w: Grand Parade on eve of Murti-Pratishtha ceremony. Five beautiful floats with the murtis of deities passed through the streets of Durban. 1,000 devotees and well wishers participated in the 2½ km procession.

Reporter, Ibrahim Patel and Cameraman Chris from the South Africa Broadcasting Corporation took a video interview of Swamishri. Q: What is the purpose of inaugurating the mandir and of what significance will it be to the residing Hindus? Swamishri: God has created the world. For the purpose of worship, the murti of God is established in a mandir. People can also offer prayers to Him and be blessed with peace of mind, good thoughts and be inspired to perform good deeds. Secondly, because of the hectic day to day activities, one is left with lingering thoughts in the mind at the end of the day. By having darshan of the Lord in the mandir, experiencing the arti and listening to the sound of bells, one’s mind becomes pacified. The mandir makes a person good. By inspiring devotion towards God, a person becomes free of his base nature, evil qualities and worldly desires and attains God’s divine abode. The mandir preserves character and righteous feelings in a person. And through the holy sadhus residing in the mandir, one gets guidance and inspiration. So through the mandir, one is exposed to and blessed with the benefits of one’s culture, dharma, scriptural reading and association with sadhus. This is the significance of mandirs and that is why they are created. Q: What is your message for the new Millennium? Swamishri: As we are approaching the new Millennium, there is one very clear statement that today man has become corrupt in so many ways. He is thinking more and more about the ways and means to attain mundane happiness. And he does this at the cost of inflicting pain and loss to thousands of people. We see a great greed for power regardless of the misunderstanding and conflict it spawns. New researches and discoveries are made to destroy people. People produce and peddle drugs and alcohol to harass mankind, to make it miserable and destroy it. For the New Year one should endeavor to free oneself from addictions, vices and base nature. (swabhavas). Man should strive to earn money rather than kill someone for it. May people respect and love each other. We also wish that there should be projects that inspire peaceful coexistence and publication of wholesome literature. To enhance faith in God more mandirs should be established, people should study the holy scriptures, respect and love the holy saints - when such feelings arise in people then the country will benefit and progress all the more..."

Despite the fact that Swamishri was recovering after the previous day's bout of temperature, he had engaged himself in a meeting today. During lunch, a sadhu requested, "During illness you have to take rest. How can you get rest when you get engaged in one meeting after another?"
Swamishri replied, "Do you consider only sleeping as a form of rest? Look I am sitting here and am very much at ease. See how restful it is."
A sadhu added, "But one has to strain one's mind in a meeting."
Another sadhu elaborated, "Conducting meetings during illness is strainful for both body and mind. You have to think to make decisions. It is all stressful."

Swamishri replied, "One feels the stress if one takes it upon himself. Look, I just take it and put it away like this. (Swamishri took a towel from one side and placed it on the other side of his sofa.) I entrust it all to Maharaj. So where is the burden or stress! No matter what number of meetings and discussions I have, I hand it over to Maharaj. People live in tension because they burden themselves with their own worries and that of others'. And do I have any tension! People come with their pains and problems to me, but I do not take it upon my head. I simply entrust it like this. The moment I lie down I go to sleep instantly... Maharaj is the all-doer."

In spite of all his efforts in the Sanstha's activities, Swamishri's working strategy of entrusting everything to Shriji Maharaj and believing Him to be the all doer is the secret of his success and unfading experience of bliss.
A spiritual discourse should be listened to thoughtfully and with attention. One should also reflect upon every word.
On becoming brahmarup, one is cured of the disease of birth and death.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
1 Aug 2002, Amdavad
250 devotees had pilgrimaged on foot from Gandhinagar to Amdavad (22 km), departing at 11.00 p.m. The devotees chanted the Swaminarayan dhun during the 7 hr pilgrimage.
Mrugesh Parmar, a teenager, had performed 2,500 prostrations from his home in Sabarmati to the mandir in Shahibaug (7.5 km).
Many devotees had pilgrimaged on foot from Randheja to Amdavad mandir (27 km).
11 Aug 2002, Amdavad
Three kishores cycled from Vadodara to Amdavad (125 km).
Two youths pilgrimaged on foot from Vihar village to Amdavad (75 km).
15 Aug 2002, Amdavad

165 students of Akshar Purushottam Chhatralay, Vidyanagar, were blessed by Swamishri for having performed various austerities for one month: 120 observed dharna-parna, 5 did khatras, 36 stayed on liquid only, 8 did shishu chandrayan and 1 dharna- parna with liquid only.
Four balaks pilgrimaged on foot from Nikol to the Swaminarayan Mandir, Shahibaug (10 km).

On this auspicious day, His Divine Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated the second traditional Hindu mandir in the United States in Bartlett, Illinois. After performing his morning puja, Swamishri made his way to the main entrance of the mandir complex where he released red and white balloons that represent colors of peace and are the official colors of the BAPS flag.

Saints and kishores dressed in traditional Indian wear lined up on two sides as Swamishri made his way to the majestic mandir. At the top, Swamishri released doves that symbolized the spread of peace around the world. After Swamishri officially opened the main doors of the mandir, he made his way inside to perform the murti prathistha ceremony in accordance with Vedic rituals.

After instilling the spirit of God into the murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan; Aksharbrahm Gunatitanand Swami; Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj; Shri Harikrishna Maharaj; Shri Radha-Krishna Dev; the Guru Parampara; Shri Sita-Ram and Hanumanji; and Shri Shiv-Parvati and Ganeshji, Swamishri blessed the yajmans present in the mandir and Haveli. Swamishri said that God has now resided in the mandir and whatever one prays for will come true. In addition, he stated, "What could not be accomplished in infinite births has been accomplished in this birth and in this body."

Dignitaries praise the organisation's work

On 8 August, P. K. Lahiri, chairman of the Narmada Nigam and former Chief Secretary of the State of Gujarat, Chhatrasinh Mori, Minister of Supplies, and Jhalavadiya Saheb, District Collector of Anand, came for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Speaking in the special satsang assembly held for the occasion, former Chief Secretary P. K. Lahiri said, "From 1959, for about 36 years, I served in various works of the State. On many occasions I have seen that whenever the State faced a calamity such as a cyclone, earthquake or flood, the sadhus and volunteers of the Sampradaya, with the inspiration and blessings of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, have done remarkable work. Whether it is rescue work or rebuilding work, this organisation has always been at the forefront of service. Some of the work was so hard, in desert areas where a person could not live in comfort and peace even for a day, yet by building villages they have constantly striven to give comfort and peace to people who had never experienced comfort and peace. Living in such a scorching desert area for one and a quarter to one and a half years, these sadhus and volunteers did truly wonderful work. That is why, all over the world, there is a unique feeling and special respect for this Sampradaya. And the wonder is that this organisation is run with such precision, speed and grace that even multinational companies can draw inspiration from it. Along with religious work, work here is done naturally and with a spirit of offering it completely to God. Because of that, one feels blessed here. Pramukh Swami Maharaj also came to the Narmada dam and performed puja, and in Ahmedabad he performed abhishek with its water and obliged us with his blessings. He has constantly been concerned that this project be completed at the earliest."

On this occasion Chhatrasinh Mori, refreshing his old memories with Swamishri, said, "It is truly wonderful that Pramukh Swami Maharaj is working in society while keeping dharma with him. There are many sampradayas, but this Sampradaya is doing the work of bringing humanity. There are very few organisations like this that serve society while preserving values. I believe that this Sampradaya is a centre of devotion. Only if humanity first comes into a person does devotion become possible. This Sampradaya is doing that work. Along with dharma, it has brought a social revolution and made a very great contribution to the upliftment of society. Along with the work of helping everyone in calamities, the satsangis also constantly try to remove the vices and evils spread through society. The work of reforming those who have gone astray, which even parents cannot do, Swamiji, the sadhus and the volunteers do. This Sampradaya is a social force. A wonderful work of social revolution is being done through Swamishri. Work has been done by this organisation in every field, the very goals the government is trying to achieve."

At 11.50 am, after the blessings had ended, Swamishri went up to his residence. Brij Joshi, a well known musician of Anand, had come for darshan. He said to Swamishri, "In the discourse just now you said that one should not have ego about any accomplishment gained through spiritual practice. You told the example of Ramakrishna Paramahansa. You spoke beautifully. Please bless me too so that I do not get ego about my accomplishment." Swamishri immediately said, "Whatever effort you make, make it only to please God, and ego will never come. If the one God is pleased, everyone is pleased. The Pandavs kept Krishna pleased. God alone is worth pleasing. Keep Him pleased, and ego will never come."

With the floods in Surat, Swamishri remained in contact with BAPS sadhus at the Surat Mandir, guiding them and praying for the waters to abate.

This morning, prior to his puja, while Swamishri was engaged in Thakorji’s darshan he instructed to start chanting the Swaminarayan dhun for the flood waters to recede and no further loss of lives and damage to property occurs. Sadhus and devotees chanted dhun before Thakorji till 12 noon. Then the chanting continued from 12.00 noon to 4.00 pm in the assembly hall. And finally the dhun was continued till 7.00 pm before Thakorji in the mandir.

At 10.45 am Swamishri got news that the water level in Surat Mandir was rising. Swamishri reassured the sadhus that everyone was praying for the waters to subside and for no further loss of lives in the city. In the evening, on Swamishri’s instruction, 20 BAPS volunteers of Valsad, formerly fishermen, set off towards Surat with a large motorboat, food packets, drinking water and other relief materials for distribution. Swamishri had also instructed sadhus at Navsari mandir to prepare food packets.
At 7.00 pm Swamishri attended the satsang assembly during which the balaks-kishores of UK made several stage presentations.

Swamishri blessed the assembly after his morning puja, “To serve the world people become doctors, engineers and acquire other qualifications, but Yogiji Maharaj said that Satsang is the college of brahmavidya. God has blessed us with a human birth, so we should live and endeavour in such a way that God and his Sadhu are pleased and grant us moksha. Human birth is not for enjoying the worldly sense pleasures. Our culture teaches us to respect our parents, teachers and guests.” Swamishri further added that one should not keep bad company, and as satsangis follow the Shikshapatri and understand the knowledge of Akshar-Purushottam according to the Vachanamrut.

After darshan, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was passing through the mandir courtyard. Some children were standing there. Among them, a little child came forward towards Swamishri with a bunch of flowers. As soon as a volunteer noticed, the little child was pushed back. The innocent child had no idea what to do. He had the bunch of flowers in his hand. Understanding the situation, Swamishri immediately and very lovingly gestured to the child and told him to go and place the bouquet before the panchmurti (five murtis) of Thakorji enshrined nearby. The child was delighted and offered the bouquet at Thakorji's feet.
Swamishri certainly understands people's minds, but along with that, in any tangle or any situation, he has always kept offering an alternative, so that everyone who makes an effort is comforted.

Anandpriya Swami phoned from London. A cricket tournament had been held in London between the various BAPS youth mandals of the UK. In this tournament it rained on the very day of the final. Speaking about this, Anandpriya Swami said, "We had prayed that it would not rain, but still..."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "God did well, he cooled things down. It was humid, so God would cool things down, wouldn't he! It must have been Maharaj's wish, so that is what happened!"
Anandpriya Swami said, "He kept it sunny all week, and this happened only at the final."

Swamishri said, "In any situation, see only the good in God. He cooled things down. We sit in the refuge of God, so things happen only according to his wish, and we should act only according to his wish."

At night, after his meal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was signing letters. It was time to go and rest. His attendant sadhus had come. Even though the rostrum placed in front of Swamishri had been taken away, Swamishri kept on writing letters. While signing the letters, Swamishri said, "There are only two letters left now, aren't there! Let us finish them."
Dharmacharan Swami said, "There are many letters, but it is now time to rest."
Swamishri said, "There are only two letters, aren't there! Let us finish them."
Dharmacharan Swami said, "It is not two, it is seven or eight, and there are others too."
Although those letters could not be signed, everyone had a wonderful glimpse of how Swamishri stays at work until the last second of the set time.

In today's assembly there was a Children's Day programme. The children played the "Best Friend Game" with Mahant Swami Maharaj. In it the children asked Swamishri questions, and Swamishri wrote the answers on an iPad, which were shown on the screen:
1. What do you pray for in your puja?
"I thank Swami and Shriji."
What is your favourite dish? "Kankoda (spiny gourd)."
2. What do you do in your spare time? "Writing letters."
3. Where are you from? "From Akshardham."
4. What is the key to Akshardham like? What do we have to do for it? "Divyabhav (seeing divinity)." Then he said, "Everyone has that key."
5. (Without writing) How far is Akshardham? "You are all in Akshardham already."
6. What do you have that we do not know about?
"I have Maharaj and Swami and Pramukh Swami."
7. Who is your best friend?
"Those who keep niyam and dharma are all best friends. All the children keep niyam and dharma."
